- If sentiment is positive (≥ 0.25) and forecast is trending upward, reduce forecast slope to avoid over-optimism.  
- If sentiment is negative (≤ -0.25) and forecast is trending downward, avoid excessive downward correction — allow slight mean reversion.  
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 55), model often overcorrects downward — cap downward momentum at 50–52 to prevent overshoot.  
- When true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 58→52→54), model tends to over-predict continuation — adjust forecast to reflect 3–5 day lagged mean.  
- If sentiment is neutral (0.00) and forecast is flat, check for horizon mismatch — true outcome often exhibits 1–2 day volatility; add 1–2% volatility buffer.  
- Avoid forecasting “smooth” trends when sentiment shows recent volatility — model should allow 1–2% ± deviation in 30d horizon.
